mapping_lock.scope_note: Repository source/CI wiring observations only; no target-runtime or whole-system credit.

external_patterns.note: F2 max_queue_items plus explicit drop accounting is preferable to a blocking producer queue for perception analysis.
Latest-only replacement is sound only when the retained item satisfies the obligations of the discarded one; freshness/deadline/authority are semantic constraints, not incidental metadata.

F2 already has max_active_workers 0..4 and explicit work/control budget. Adding AnyIO only for this would add dependency/version risk, including recent limiter race fixes, without clear information gain.

current_f2_strengths: 0..4 worker policy is explicit and validates zero-worker state.
Queue size and drop accounting are bounded.
Control reserve is subtracted before perception work is admitted.
First-pass dispatch gives distinct sources a chance before second work from an already represented source.
No sensor opening, raw-frame persistence, provider invocation, truth/effect/completion authority is introduced by the scheduler.

critical_mismatches.finding: _coalesce_key() omits ObserveIntent.required_freshness_ns. Two requests for the same source/heads/atoms/ROI can be collapsed even if one requires materially fresher evidence.
critical_mismatches.risk: The stricter observation obligation can disappear before dispatch.

critical_mismatches.finding: Normal scheduling rank prefers earliest expiry after priority, but _preferred_coalesced() prefers later expiry within equal generation/priority.
critical_mismatches.risk: Coalescing can invert the scheduler's own deadline semantics and discard the request that must be satisfied sooner.

critical_mismatches.finding: permission_snapshot_sha256 is not part of coalescing equivalence. The retained request can therefore be bound to a different permission epoch than the discarded request.
critical_mismatches.risk: Dispatch-time fail-closed validation remains safe for authority, but a stale retained request can cause useful work to disappear instead of retaining a still-valid request. Safety is preserved; liveness/utility may not be.

critical_mismatches.finding: Source diversity is enforced only after the global queue has been sorted and truncated. A noisy high-ranked source with many distinct coalesce keys can fill max_queue_items and evict every pending request from another source before the fair first dispatch pass runs.
critical_mismatches.risk: N-sources-greater-than-workers remains bounded but can still exhibit source starvation.

critical_mismatches.finding: recent_dropped_intent_ids are sorted, then reused as if their order encoded recency before suffix truncation on the next enqueue.
critical_mismatches.risk: The bounded diagnostic set may not actually be the most recent N dropped IDs, weakening audit interpretation while leaving total drop count intact.

proposed_f2_shape.name: WP710_CONSTRAINT_DOMINANCE_COALESCING/v0
required_invariants: Never coalesce requests merely because payload target fields match; semantic request constraints must be compatible.
A retained/coalesced request must dominate or preserve the strictest required_freshness_ns and deadline obligations of every discarded request.
Permission snapshot epoch/digest differences are not silently erased; authority is still revalidated at actual dispatch.
Coalescing must never turn a valid stricter request into no work solely because a looser retained request later fails permission validation.
Backpressure remains bounded and must not block CaptureOwner/Broker progress.
Source fairness must be tested at admission as well as dispatch if WP710 claims anti-starvation across N sources.
Drop diagnostics must state whether retained IDs are chronological or merely a bounded sample/set.
minimal_repair_options: Conservative: include required_freshness_ns, expires_monotonic_ns and permission_snapshot_sha256 in coalescing equivalence, reducing conflation but preserving semantics.
Stronger: introduce a pure dominance relation and synthesize/retain a request that carries the strictest compatible constraints; reject conflation when constraints are incomparable.
Do not add AnyIO/ZeroMQ/GStreamer as scheduler dependencies; their useful behavior is already small enough to encode and test natively.

hypothesis.statement: The current WP710 native scheduler is architecturally preferable to importing an external scheduler, but its coalescing relation is too weak because it conflates target equivalence with obligation equivalence.

counterhypothesis.statement: An upstream invariant guarantees that later/equal-key ObserveIntents always subsume all freshness/deadline/permission obligations of earlier ones, making the current replacement rule safe.
counterhypothesis.falsifier: Create two still-valid same-target ObserveIntents with identical coalesce-key fields but different required_freshness_ns and expiry. Enqueue both and assert that the surviving state still represents the stricter obligation. A second case should vary permission snapshot digest and prove a valid request cannot be erased in favor of a stale one.

adoption_decision.handoff: Before WP710 is accepted, add exact regression cases for freshness/deadline/permission coalescing and, if anti-starvation is claimed, pre-dispatch queue admission fairness. Repair only if the executable counterexample reproduces.
